newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures bouyant, March retests hurdle.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures bouyant, March retests hurdle.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures re-tested the recent high of $1,335 a tonne, basis March, on Wednesday after a wave of trade and fund buying.
But origin-led selling pushed back values from intraday highs, although most positions still posted impressive gains by the finish.
Traders said steadier New York prices and news of port strike in key grower Colombia provided some background support.
March finished $17 firmer at $1,327 a tonne but failed to vault over the January 9 high of $1,335, seen as a key hurdle. Overhead selling, notably from origins, helped cap gains.
May, leading advancers, surged by $26 to $1,314 and helped narrow the March/May spread to $13 from the previous close of $22.
"The market saw some decent system buying coming to London which obviously pushed the market up towards the close on the highs," said one.
"We've really got to be looking now for the funds to be going long, something probably in the region of 500-1,000 lots," he added.
Turnover reached an impressive 8,112 lots, centred on March and May contracts.
A strike by Colombian dock workers has paralysed all activity in the Pacific coast port of Buenaventura, private operators said on Wednesday.
The action has effectively halted 60 percent of Colombia's coffee exports and all the country's sugar exports.
Market players are also keeping a close watch on U.S. Green Coffee Association monthly stock figures. The data, due after New York's close on Wednesday, is expected to be unchanged to slightly up.
News LIFFE certified stocks fell by 226 to 1,875 lots in December had little influence.
African producers on Wednesday urged Asian states namely Indonesia and Vietnam to back their plan to trim coffee exports.
Traders said both Indonesia and Vietnam had been lukewarm to IACO's plan for a cut in Association of Coffee Producing Countries' (ACPC) exports in the first half of 1997.
